newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico confirms death of cocaine king Carrillo.
newsitem.headline: Mexico confirms death of cocaine king Carrillo.

text.p: Mexican authorities on Thursday confirmed that the country's most powerful drug trafficker, Amado Carrillo Fuentes, was dead, ending a week of speculation about the fate of the "Lord of the Skies."
A DNA test proved that a man found dead in a Mexico City hospital under a false name last Friday was indeed Carrillo, said the head of Mexico's anti-drug agency, Mariano Herran Salvatti.
"Together with the other tests we carried out on the body, we have arrived at the definitive conclusion (the body) is that of Mr. Amado Carrillo Fuentes," Herran told a news conference.
Herran said detectives still did not know how Carrillo had died. He did not rule out foul play.
Authorities have released the body to the capo's family for an early funeral in his home state of Sinaloa in northwest Mexico, radio reports said.
The news ended a week-long drama after reports surfaced last Saturday that Carrillo had died after botched plastic surgery and liposuction in Mexico City's private Santa Monica hospital.

The fugitive drug lord's mother, Aurora Fuentes, confirmed his death on Saturday. Thomas Constantine, director of the U.S. Drug Enforcement Agency, confirmed Carrillo's death on Sunday, saying his agents had matched fingerprints from the dead capo.
But Mexico, notoriously secretive about drug issues and apparently unwilling to allow Carrillo's death to overshadow historic midterm elections held last Sunday, was slow to confirm the news.

Although the corpse was badly disfigured from the surgery, Salvatti said the body's physical characteristics matched those of the drug lord, who shipped tonnes of cocaine a year to the United States from his base in northern Mexico. He had been nicknamed "Lord of the Skies" for his brazen tactic of jetting drugs into Mexico for transshipment.

The death certificate issued for the body gave the cause of death as a heart attack, but the local Televisa television network quoted an unnamed hospital source as saying Carrillo had been murdered by one of his bodyguards while he was recovering.
Salvatti said officials had ruled out suffocation as the cause of death but did not know if Carrillo might have been murdered by other means, such as a lethal injection.
He said four doctors, three not from the hospital, had performed the surgery and two heavily armed bodyguards had kept watch over the drug lord, keeping hospital staff away.
Mexican authorities were questioning the doctors, he said.
At the drug lord's family ranch in Guamuchilito, Sinaloa, there was an immediate burst of activity as family, friends and relatives turned up within minutes of the announcement.
Scores of four-wheel drive and other luxury vehicles with dark-tinted windows arrived at high speed at the ranch. The drivers and passengers refused to answer reporters' questions.
